reviews.review: it's just kinda not that great

Aliens: Fireteam Elite is something of an under-rated gem. I think the word that describes it is "satisfying". Satisfying gunplay. Satisfying and varied classes. A satisfying perks system. Solid all round.

As a fan of the franchise, I like that it has lots of nods to the series (movies and games alike) while also carving out its own niche. The smartgun is here. The pulse gun is here. That's great. But there are also multitudes of other cool weapons to collect and customise. The flamethrower is A-tier. It roars, it destroys, it floods the screen with fire, it blasts your enemies and teammates alike, it helps you set new records for friendly fire damage. It's awesome.

You'll note this is not an [i]Alien[/i] game. This is an [i]Aliens[/i] game. The developers have really picked up on what made James Cameron's vision of the Alien universe unique and I commend them for capturing the [b]feel[/b] of [i]Aliens[/i], not just the aesthetics. 

When moving and exploring, there is a proper sense of urgency and movement, which really has a cinematic feel at times - thinking of all the scenes from the movie, rushing through tunnels eliminating targets while maintaining unit cohesion, that kind of thing. Most levels are centred around various hold-out set-pieces where you have to defend a certain location - naturally breaking out the sentry guns, scouting out the fields of fire, and other tactical operations, in a way that made me feel like an actual Colonial Marine applying battlefield doctrine. It's very impressive. Other times remind me of the disastrous first encounter from the movie, as you bungle everything and run around in panic setting your allies on fire with the flamethrower, which is, as I mentioned, a great flamethrower.

But it does all this with just enough new lore and story that makes this game something new. Very cool.
